body.statement: For every balanced sequence \(m=m(n)\) with \(m\to\infty\), \(N\to\infty\), and \(m/n\to0\), and every interior \(\beta_0\in\mathcal K^{\circ}\), \[\lim_{c\to\infty}\lim_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\delta_m}\sup_{\substack{\beta=\beta_0+(h,u)/\sqrt m\in\mathcal K,\ h\in\mathbb R^r,\ u\in\mathbb R^s\\\lVert(h,u)\rVert\le c}}nm\,(N/n)^2E\{V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\delta_m,\beta)-V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(G_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\beta),\beta)\}=B(\beta_0).\] The infimum ranges over all pilot-measurable normalized centered score rules. The rule \(\widehat G_m\) satisfies \[\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}\left|nm\,(N/n)^2E\{V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\widehat G_m,\beta)-V_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(G_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\beta),\beta)\}-B(\beta)\right|\to0,\] where expectations include the random complement and pilot outcomes, and \(B(\beta)=\operatorname{tr}\{\Gamma(\beta)I_{\mathrm{eff}}(\beta)^{-1}\}\) uses the continuous coarea boundary covariance of \(G_{\infty}\).
body.justification: The trace constant converts nuisance-efficient pilot information into the unavoidable quadratic loss from selecting a rerandomization geometry.
body.gap: Liu, Han, Rubin, and Deng integrate over prior uncertainty, and Armstrong gives first-order superpopulation efficiency bounds; neither derives this finite-population exact-alpha local design game.
body.consumer: It identifies which pilot outcomes and nuisance directions determine the precision value of another learning batch.

obligation.what_is_open: The uniform local asymptotic minimax transfer from the adaptive pilot experiment to exact finite Horvitz--Thompson action loss for arbitrary measurable actions.
obligation.obstruction: Quadratic-mean differentiability and information regularity identify the candidate Gaussian shift, but they do not by themselves establish a uniformly efficient pilot estimator with quadratic-loss uniform integrability, localization of unrestricted actions, or the shrinking finite-boundary comparison.
obligation.attempted: Derived the outcome-only likelihood architecture and the Gaussian boundary Hessian. The remaining bridge is precisely the finite comparison plus uniform decision-theoretic localization, so assuming the trace constant would assume the theorem's crux.
obligation.partial_result:
The fixed-baseline and product-law assumptions imply that the pilot likelihood ratio contains only the \(m\) revealed conditional outcome likelihood ratios.  Under the stated quadratic-mean differentiability conditions its formal central sequence is
\[
\Delta_m=m^{-1/2}\sum_{i\in S_m}
s_{Z_i,\beta}(Y_{in}(Z_i)\mid x_{in}),
\]
with nuisance-efficient information \(I_{\mathrm{eff}}\).  The Gaussian boundary calculation makes the candidate quadratic action loss equal to
\(h^{\mathsf T}\Gamma(\beta)h\), so an efficient Gaussian shift would give
\[
\operatorname{tr}\{\Gamma(\beta)I_{\mathrm{eff}}(\beta)^{-1}\}.
\]
What is not established is the uniform triangular-array local-asymptotic-normality-to-decision transfer together with the exact finite Horvitz--Thompson boundary comparison for unrestricted measurable actions.
